Yes — if your deciding priorities are avoiding **new long-lived nuclear waste**, avoiding a **large construction cost/sunk-cost risk**, and trusting that blackouts can be managed through grid interconnections, renewables, efficiency, and storage, then voting to **keep the ban on new nuclear power plants** is a coherent and defensible choice.

The only caveat is that “no contest” is a bit strong: blackout risk, grid resilience, and climate arguments are real counterpoints. But as a value-based judgment, your reasoning supports your vote: **yes, it confirms your position.**

But also note "the 'no contest' framing leaves out counterarguments; a fair confirmation: it's a value judgment." Need perhaps provide concise.

But it isn't objectively 'no contest'—blackout risk, climate, grid stability are tradeoffs. Switzerland can still manage with imports, renewables, storage, etc. So if you want to vote yes, you can do so on those grounds."

Need likely mention "new nuclear" not existing. "Keep the ban" means vote for Anti-Atom? Yes.

Need maybe include a simple ballot statement: "I vote yes because I prioritize avoiding new nuclear waste and large sunk costs, and I trust grid flexibility/imports more than building new nuclear capacity." Good.

Let's craft final with empathetic confirmation but nuance. User asked "Just confirm it for me."
